flashcards.bulk: Paste many cards, one per line as "front - back"
flashcards.importCsv: Import a CSV file or drop it here
flashcards.storeNote: Cards are stored in this browser and are not sent to a server. Export a CSV to back them up.
flashcards.confirmDelete: Delete this deck and all the cards in it?
flashcards.study.allDone: You have reviewed every card that was due. Well done!
flashcards.study.empty: This deck has no cards yet. Go to Cards in deck to add some.
flashcards.study.tap: Tap the card to flip it
flashcards.noSpeech: This browser does not support text to speech.
flashcards.quiz.need: You need at least 4 cards with different answers to take a quiz.
flashcards.noneAdded: No valid cards found. Each line needs two parts separated by a dash.
flashcards.needBoth: Enter both the front and the back.
flashcards.confirmReset: Reset the study progress of every card in this deck?
flashcards.seo.how1: Create a deck by pasting several lines in the form "front - back" or by adding cards one at a time. You can also import a CSV file and export it again to back it up or use it elsewhere.
flashcards.seo.how2: While studying, tap the card to flip it and see the answer, then choose Got it or Not yet. A card you remembered moves to a higher box and is scheduled further out; a card you forgot goes back to the first box to be reviewed again right away.
flashcards.seo.how3: Quiz mode builds four-choice questions from your own deck. The listen button reads the card aloud with your browser voice, and you can choose the language.
flashcards.faq.q1: How do flashcards help with learning vocabulary?
flashcards.faq.a1: Trying to recall the answer before flipping the card strengthens memory more than simply rereading. Reviewing at growing intervals helps you remember for longer in less time.
flashcards.faq.q2: What is the Leitner box system?
flashcards.faq.a2: It sorts cards into boxes. A card you remember moves up a box and is reviewed less often, after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days; a card you forget goes back to the first box.
flashcards.faq.q3: How do I import a list of words I already have?
flashcards.faq.a3: Paste lines made of two parts separated by a dash, a colon, a semicolon or a Tab, or choose a two-column CSV file.
flashcards.faq.a4: In your browser, never on a server. Export a CSV to back it up before you clear browser data or change devices.
flashcards.faq.q5: How does the pronunciation feature work?
flashcards.faq.a5: It uses the voice built into your browser or operating system. Choose the deck language so the right voice is used; some languages need the matching voice to be installed on your device.

media-trim-convert.dropTitle: Choose an audio or video file, or drop it here
media-trim-convert.dropHint: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG… Up to 1 GB.
media-trim-convert.fast: Fast trim, keeps the original quality (the cut point may be off by a few seconds)
media-trim-convert.note: Processed in your browser with ffmpeg, so your file is not uploaded to a server. The first run downloads the processor, about 31 MB. Only process files you have the right to use.
media-trim-convert.needVideo: This action needs a video file.
media-trim-convert.tooBig: The file is larger than 1 GB and the browser does not have enough memory to process it.
media-trim-convert.badTime: Invalid time. Use minutes:seconds, for example 1:30; the end must be after the start.
media-trim-convert.gifLong: A GIF should be shorter than 60 seconds. Choose a shorter part.
media-trim-convert.failed: This file could not be processed. It may be damaged or in an unsupported format.
media-trim-convert.seo.howTitle: How to trim and convert audio and video
media-trim-convert.seo.how1: Choose a file, preview it, then enter the start and end points or use the current player position. Fast trim keeps the original quality and is very quick, but the cut point may be off by a few seconds; precise trimming re-encodes the file.
media-trim-convert.seo.how2: The Convert format tab turns video into MP4 or WebM, and turns audio, or the sound track of a video, into MP3, M4A, WAV or OGG, with three quality levels.
media-trim-convert.seo.how3: The Video to GIF tab makes an animated image from part of a video, with a choice of frames per second and width. Everything uses ffmpeg running inside your browser, so your files are never sent anywhere.
media-trim-convert.faq.q1: Does trimming a video reduce its quality?
media-trim-convert.faq.a1: Fast trim copies the data as it is, so quality is unchanged. Precise trim re-encodes the video, so quality depends on the level you choose.
media-trim-convert.faq.q2: Why is the fast trim point a little off?
media-trim-convert.faq.a2: Fast trim can only cut at the video keyframes, so the clip may start slightly earlier. Use precise trim when you need an exact second.
media-trim-convert.faq.q3: Is my file uploaded to a server?
media-trim-convert.faq.a3: No. All processing happens in your browser. The first time, it downloads the ffmpeg processor, about 31 MB, and later your browser reuses it.
media-trim-convert.faq.q4: What is the file size limit?
media-trim-convert.faq.a4: Up to 1 GB, but big files need a lot of memory and run slowly. For long videos, trim first or use a computer instead of a phone.
media-trim-convert.faq.q5: Which format should I convert to?
media-trim-convert.faq.a5: MP4 plays on almost every device, WebM is light for the web, MP3 is the most common audio format, and WAV is uncompressed so it keeps original quality but is large.

base64-text.sample: Hello WFTools! This tool runs right in your browser.
base64-text.decNote: Automatically detects standard Base64, Base64URL (using - and _) and data:...;base64, strings, with or without = padding.
base64-text.binary: (Binary data, not text. Click "Save as file" to download it)
base64-text.bad: This is not a valid Base64 string. Check for stray characters or a truncated part.
base64-text.seo.howTitle: What is Base64 and how to use this tool
base64-text.seo.how1: Base64 represents any data using 64 safe characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, + and /). It is commonly used to embed images in HTML/CSS, send email attachments or carry binary data inside JSON.
base64-text.seo.how2: The Encode tab converts text to Base64 using UTF-8, so accented and non-English characters come through intact. Choose Base64URL when the string goes into a link or a JWT token.
base64-text.seo.how3: The Decode tab automatically handles strings with or without = padding and data URIs. If the result is binary data, you can save it as a file.
base64-text.faq.q1: Is Base64 a form of secure encryption?
base64-text.faq.a1: No. Base64 is just a way of rewriting data, and anyone can decode it. To keep data secret, use the AES Encryption tool.
base64-text.faq.q2: Why is a Base64 string longer than the original text?
base64-text.faq.a2: Every 3 bytes of data are written as 4 characters, so the size grows by about 33%.
base64-text.faq.q3: How is Base64URL different from standard Base64?
base64-text.faq.a3: Base64URL replaces + with - and / with _, and usually drops the trailing = so it is safe in links and file names.
base64-text.faq.q4: What if the decoded text looks garbled?
base64-text.faq.a4: The original data may not be UTF-8, or it may be a binary file. Click Save as file and open it with the right program.
base64-text.faq.q5: Is there a file size limit?
base64-text.faq.a5: There is no fixed limit, but files over a few dozen MB may slow down your browser because everything is processed in your device's memory.

url-encode.note: Type in the left box to encode, or paste a string containing %XX into the right box and click Decode. Accented characters are converted to UTF-8.
url-encode.bad: The string contains an invalid % character (it must be % followed by 2 hex digits, such as %20). Fix the problem and try again.
url-encode.seo.how1: Links can only contain certain characters. Accented letters, spaces, & or ? inside a parameter value must be converted to percent form such as %20 so browsers and servers understand them correctly.
url-encode.seo.how2: Component mode is for parameter values (after the = sign). Full URL mode keeps structural characters such as : / ? & # unchanged.
url-encode.seo.how3: Form data mode turns spaces into + signs, the same way a browser submits a form as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
url-encode.faq.q1: What is the difference between %20 and the + sign?
url-encode.faq.a1: Both mean a space. %20 works in any part of a URL, while + only means a space in a form query string.
url-encode.faq.q2: Why does my link turn into something like %C3%A9?
url-encode.faq.a2: Browsers encode accented characters as UTF-8, turning each one into 2 to 3 %XX groups. Paste that string into the right box and click Decode to read it again.
url-encode.faq.q3: Should I use encodeURI or encodeURIComponent?
url-encode.faq.a3: Use encodeURIComponent for each parameter value, and encodeURI for a whole link when you only want to convert accented letters and spaces.
url-encode.faq.q4: What does the invalid % error mean when decoding?
url-encode.faq.a4: The string has a % sign that is not followed by exactly 2 hex digits, for example 50%. Change it to %25 or remove the stray % sign.
url-encode.faq.q5: Is the data I paste sent anywhere?
url-encode.faq.a5: No. Encoding and decoding run entirely in JavaScript on your device.

hash-gen.fileNote: Use this to check whether a downloaded file matches the hash published by its vendor.
hash-gen.match: Matches {a}. The file or text is exactly as published.
hash-gen.noMatch: No algorithm matches. The data has been changed, or you are comparing against the wrong algorithm.
hash-gen.seo.how1: A hash function turns any data into a string of fixed length. Change a single character and the hash changes completely, so it is used to check whether a file was corrupted or altered during download.
hash-gen.seo.how2: Software vendors often publish a SHA-256 hash next to the download. Choose the file on the Hash file tab, paste the published hash into the compare box, and the tool tells you right away whether they match.
hash-gen.seo.how3: MD5 and SHA-1 are no longer safe against deliberate forgery, but they still work well for catching transfer errors. When security matters, use SHA-256 or stronger.
hash-gen.faq.q1: Can a hash be reversed to the original text?
hash-gen.faq.a1: No. Hashing is one-way. Sites that claim to decrypt MD5 simply look the hash up in a database of common passwords that were hashed in advance.
hash-gen.faq.q2: Is a large file uploaded when I hash it?
hash-gen.faq.a2: No. The file is read and hashed right in your browser, even files of several GB (depending on your device memory).
hash-gen.faq.q3: Why is my result different from another machine?
hash-gen.faq.a3: Check for spaces, trailing line breaks and the character encoding. This tool hashes strings as UTF-8.
hash-gen.faq.q4: Should I store passwords with MD5 or SHA-256?
hash-gen.faq.a4: No. Passwords need a slow, salted algorithm such as bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2.
hash-gen.faq.q5: How is CRC32 different from SHA?
hash-gen.faq.a5: CRC32 is very fast and only 8 characters long. It is used to detect random errors (ZIP files, networks), not for security.

jwt-decode.bad: This is not a JWT: it must have 3 parts separated by dots (xxx.yyy.zzz).
jwt-decode.badJson: The header or payload could not be decoded as JSON. The token may have been cut off when copied.
jwt-decode.algNo: This token uses the {a} algorithm: only HMAC signatures (HS256/384/512) can be verified, using a secret key.
jwt-decode.sigOk: The signature is valid for this key.
jwt-decode.sigBad: The signature does not match: the secret key is wrong or the token has been altered.
jwt-decode.seo.how1: A JWT has 3 parts separated by dots: the header (algorithm), the payload (user info, permissions, expiry) and the signature. The first two are just JSON written in Base64URL, so anyone can read them.
jwt-decode.seo.how2: This tool decodes the first two parts, formats them neatly and converts the exp, iat and nbf timestamps into readable dates and times, along with whether the token is still valid or expired.
jwt-decode.seo.how3: For tokens signed with HMAC (HS256, HS384, HS512), enter the secret key to check that the signature is valid, meaning the token was not altered and was truly issued by your server.
jwt-decode.faq.q1: Is it safe to paste a real token here?
jwt-decode.faq.a1: The token is processed entirely in your browser and never sent anywhere. Even so, do not share a live token with others, because it may let them sign in as you.
jwt-decode.faq.q2: Why can anyone read the payload?
jwt-decode.faq.a2: The payload is only Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted. Never put passwords or sensitive data in a JWT.
jwt-decode.faq.a3: exp is the expiry time in seconds since January 1, 1970 (Unix time). After this moment the server must reject the token.
jwt-decode.faq.q4: Can I verify an RS256 token?
jwt-decode.faq.a4: The tool can read the contents of RS256 and ES256 tokens, but it only verifies signatures for HMAC algorithms that use a shared secret key.
jwt-decode.faq.q5: The tool says the token cannot be decoded. Why?
jwt-decode.faq.a5: It is usually caused by missing characters or by extra text such as Bearer or quotation marks when copying. The tool removes a leading Bearer automatically.

html-entities.m.all: Convert all non-ASCII characters to numeric codes (é)
html-entities.note: Encoding lets you show HTML code as plain text on a web page (so the browser does not run it). Decoding turns &lt; &#233; … back into real characters.
html-entities.seo.how1: An HTML entity is a way to write a character as a code, for example < for the < sign or © for ©. This lets you display HTML code on a web page without the browser running it.
html-entities.seo.how2: Basic mode converts only the 5 characters that have special meaning in HTML. Named entity mode also converts common symbols such as € ™ — into readable names.
html-entities.seo.how3: Numeric mode converts every non-ASCII character, including accented letters, into &#number; form, so it works even on legacy systems that do not support UTF-8.
html-entities.faq.q1: When do I need to encode entities?
html-entities.faq.a1: When putting user-entered content on a web page, writing tutorials that include HTML code, or inserting text into HTML attributes.
html-entities.faq.a2: Encoding the 5 characters & < > double quote and single quote is an important step against code injection, but it depends on context (inside scripts and URLs you need other methods).
html-entities.faq.a3: It is a non-breaking space, which keeps two words on the same line.
html-entities.faq.q4: Do I need to encode accented letters?
html-entities.faq.a4: Not if your page uses UTF-8. Only encode them when the target system does not support UTF-8.
html-entities.faq.q5: Does decoding support the hex form A?
html-entities.faq.a5: Yes. The tool decodes named entities, decimal numbers like A and hex like A.

uuid-gen.inspect: Paste a UUID/ULID to inspect it
uuid-gen.notId: Not a UUID (32 hex digits) or ULID (26 characters).
uuid-gen.seo.howTitle: Choosing the right kind of identifier
uuid-gen.seo.how1: A UUID is a 128-bit ID made of 32 hex digits, with a practically zero chance of collision. UUID v4 is completely random, which suits order IDs, session IDs and primary keys.
uuid-gen.seo.how2: UUID v7 and ULID put the creation time at the front, so they sort in time order, which helps databases write faster when used as primary keys.
uuid-gen.seo.how3: Paste an ID into the inspect box to see which UUID version it is and, for UUID v7 or ULID, when it was created.
uuid-gen.faq.a1: In theory yes, but with UUID v4 you would need to generate about 2.7 quintillion IDs to have a 50% chance of a single duplicate pair.
uuid-gen.faq.q2: Should I use UUID v4 or v7?
uuid-gen.faq.a2: Use v7 for database primary keys so indexes stay compact and fast. Use v4 when you do not want to reveal the creation time.
uuid-gen.faq.a3: A ULID is a 26-character ID (Crockford Base32 alphabet) whose first 10 characters are a timestamp. It is shorter and easier to read than a UUID.
uuid-gen.faq.a4: GUID is Microsoft's name for UUID. The format is the same, often written in uppercase and wrapped in curly braces.
uuid-gen.faq.a5: Yes. The tool uses your browser's crypto.getRandomValues, the same randomness source used for encryption.

aes-encrypt.pwNote: Remember your password: there is no way to recover the data if you forget it. Use a long, hard-to-guess password.
aes-encrypt.sample: Secret note: the safe combination is 2468.
aes-encrypt.algo: Algorithm: AES-256-GCM, with the key derived from your password using PBKDF2-SHA256 at 200,000 iterations, and a random salt and IV for every encryption.
aes-encrypt.wrong: Decryption failed: the password is wrong, or the data was not encrypted by this tool or has been altered.
aes-encrypt.seo.how1: Your password is stretched into a 256-bit key using PBKDF2-SHA256 over 200,000 iterations with a random salt, which makes password guessing extremely slow.
aes-encrypt.seo.how2: Data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, the standard used by banks and messaging apps. GCM also detects if even a single byte of the data has been altered.
aes-encrypt.seo.how3: Encrypted text is output as Base64 so you can paste it into emails and messages. Files are saved with the .wftenc extension and decrypted again with this same tool.
aes-encrypt.faq.q1: Can I recover my data if I forget the password?
aes-encrypt.faq.a1: No. There is no back door, and we cannot open it either. Remember the password or store it in a password manager.
aes-encrypt.faq.q2: Is it safe to send encrypted text by email or chat?
aes-encrypt.faq.a2: Yes, as long as the password is strong and you share the password through a different channel (a phone call or in person).
aes-encrypt.faq.q3: Is it a bug that the result is different every time?
aes-encrypt.faq.a3: It is not a bug. The random salt and IV make the output different each time, but decryption still gives back the same content.
aes-encrypt.faq.a4: Yes, but files are processed in memory, so keep them under a few hundred MB on a phone.
aes-encrypt.faq.q5: Can I open a .wftenc file with other software?
aes-encrypt.faq.a5: The format is 4 bytes of WFT1, a 16-byte salt, a 12-byte IV, then the AES-GCM data. Developers can decrypt it themselves with standard libraries.

hmac-gen.use: HMAC is commonly used to verify webhooks (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, payment gateways): the sender signs the content with a shared key, and the receiver signs it again and compares.
hmac-gen.badKey: The key does not match the chosen format (hex contains only 0-9, a-f).
hmac-gen.match: Match: the content is intact and came from a party holding the key.
hmac-gen.noMatch: No match: wrong key, wrong algorithm, or the content has been altered.
hmac-gen.seo.how1: HMAC is a signature created from a message and a shared secret key. The receiver signs the message again with the same key. If the two signatures match, the message was not altered and came from the right sender.
hmac-gen.seo.how2: Services such as Stripe, GitHub, Shopify and payment gateways sign their webhooks with HMAC. Paste the exact body you received and the key here to test.
hmac-gen.seo.how3: Choose the key format (text, hex, Base64) and output format exactly as the service documentation requires, because the wrong format produces a completely different signature.
hmac-gen.faq.q1: Why doesn't my signature match the service's?
hmac-gen.faq.a1: It is usually because whitespace in the body changed, the JSON field order changed, or the algorithm or hex/Base64 format is wrong. You must sign the exact original string you received.
hmac-gen.faq.q2: How is HMAC different from a SHA-256 hash?
hmac-gen.faq.a2: Anyone can compute SHA-256, but HMAC needs a secret key, so only someone holding the key can produce the correct signature.
hmac-gen.faq.q3: Is my secret key exposed when I paste it here?
hmac-gen.faq.a3: No. All calculations run in your browser using Web Crypto and nothing is sent anywhere.
hmac-gen.faq.q4: How do I compare a GitHub signature with the sha256= prefix?
hmac-gen.faq.a4: Paste the whole string into the compare box. The tool automatically removes the sha256= prefix when comparing.
hmac-gen.faq.a5: Only when a legacy system requires it. For new systems, use HMAC-SHA256 or stronger.

cipher-tools.note: Caesar, ROT13, Vigenère and Atbash only change the letters A-Z and leave numbers and punctuation unchanged. Morse strips accents before encoding. These ciphers are for learning and puzzles, and are not secure enough to protect real data.
cipher-tools.bad: Cannot decode: the data is not in the format of the selected cipher.
cipher-tools.seo.how1: The Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a number of steps in the alphabet, and ROT13 is a Caesar shift of 13. Vigenère uses a keyword so each letter shifts by a different amount, making it harder to guess.
cipher-tools.seo.how2: Morse code represents letters with dots and dashes, with words separated by /. Accented letters are converted to plain letters before encoding.
cipher-tools.seo.how3: Binary and hex convert each UTF-8 byte of the text into a string of 0s and 1s or into hexadecimal, which is handy when learning computer science basics.
cipher-tools.faq.a1: No. There are only 25 possible shifts, so all of them can be tried in seconds. Use it only for games and scouting-style secret messages.
cipher-tools.faq.q2: How do I decode a Caesar cipher when I don't know the shift?
cipher-tools.faq.a2: Try shifts from 1 to 25 in the Shift amount box until the text makes sense.
cipher-tools.faq.q3: What separates words in Morse code?
cipher-tools.faq.a3: Letters are separated by one space, and words by a / (or three spaces).
cipher-tools.faq.q4: Why do accents disappear in Morse code?
cipher-tools.faq.a4: International Morse has no accented letters, so the tool converts them to unaccented letters.
cipher-tools.faq.q5: Is there a cipher that is safe for real use?
cipher-tools.faq.a5: Use the AES Encryption tool with a strong password.

unicode-inspect.warnInv: Hidden characters were found. They can break string comparisons, usernames or source code.
unicode-inspect.warnNfc: The text contains decomposed accented letters (NFD). It is best to normalize it to NFC.
unicode-inspect.seo.how1: Strings that look identical can contain hidden characters such as a zero-width space (U+200B) or text direction marks, causing failed logins, searches that find nothing or strange source code errors.
unicode-inspect.seo.how2: Accented letters can be stored in two ways: precomposed (NFC) and decomposed (NFD, a base letter plus a separate accent mark). Text copied from macOS or PDFs is often NFD, so normalize it to NFC.
unicode-inspect.seo.how3: The stats show visible characters, code points, JavaScript length and UTF-8 bytes, so you can check database length limits, SMS or tweet limits.
unicode-inspect.faq.q1: Why is the string length different from the number of characters I see?
unicode-inspect.faq.a1: Emoji and some characters take 2 UTF-16 units or are made of several combined code points, so different ways of counting give different results.
unicode-inspect.faq.q2: Where do hidden characters come from?
unicode-inspect.faq.a2: Usually from copying out of web pages, Word, PDFs or chat apps. Click Remove hidden characters to clean the text.
unicode-inspect.faq.q3: Does NFC normalization change the content?
unicode-inspect.faq.a3: It does not change the visible text, only how it is stored, so programs compare and search it accurately.
unicode-inspect.faq.q4: How many bytes does an accented letter take?
unicode-inspect.faq.a4: Usually 2 to 3 bytes in UTF-8, while plain unaccented letters take just 1 byte.
unicode-inspect.faq.a5: The detail table shows up to the first 2,000 characters, but the stats are still calculated on the entire text.

string-escape.note: Use this when you need to paste text with quotes, line breaks or backslashes into source code, a SQL statement or a regex without breaking the syntax.
string-escape.bad: The string has an escape sequence that is invalid for this context. Check for a missing \ or quote.
string-escape.seo.how1: In source code some characters have special meaning: a quote ends a string, a \ starts a special character, and a line break ends a line. Escaping writes them in a special way so the content stays intact.
string-escape.seo.how2: Choose the right context because each language has its own rules: SQL doubles single quotes, CSV wraps cells in double quotes, and Regex adds \ before . * + ? and brackets.
string-escape.seo.how3: The Unescape button does the reverse, turning strings from logs, JSON files or source code back into the original text.
string-escape.faq.q1: Does escaping a SQL string prevent SQL injection?
string-escape.faq.a1: It helps avoid syntax errors, but the safest approach is still to use parameterized statements (prepared statements).
string-escape.faq.q2: Why do Windows paths need two backslashes?
string-escape.faq.a2: In JSON and JavaScript a single \ starts a special character, so you must write \\ to get one real backslash.
string-escape.faq.a3: When you want to match a string that contains characters such as . or ( ) literally, without them taking on special meaning.
string-escape.faq.q4: How is a shell command escaped?
string-escape.faq.a4: The string is wrapped in single quotes, and any single quote inside is written by closing the string, adding an escaped quote and reopening it.
string-escape.faq.a5: Yes. When unescaping JavaScript style, the tool understands \uXXXX, \u{...} and \xXX.

lorem-ipsum.start: Start with "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet…"
lorem-ipsum.note: Lorem ipsum is placeholder Latin text used to fill space when designing interfaces, print layouts and website mockups before the real content is ready.
lorem-ipsum.seo.how1: Lorem Ipsum is meaningless Latin text that designers and printers have used for centuries to fill empty space, so viewers focus on the layout instead of reading the content.
lorem-ipsum.seo.how2: Choose a quantity and a unit (paragraphs, sentences, words, list items). The tool generates different random text every time, with natural sentence lengths like real writing.
lorem-ipsum.seo.how3:
Choose the HTML format to get ready-made

or

  • tags, or Markdown to paste into documents and READMEs.
lorem-ipsum.faq.a1: The text is adapted from a Latin philosophical work by Cicero, but it has been scrambled so it no longer has meaning.
lorem-ipsum.faq.q2: Do I need to credit a source?
lorem-ipsum.faq.a2: No. Lorem Ipsum is free text you can use however you like.
lorem-ipsum.faq.q3: Why not use real text for mockups?
lorem-ipsum.faq.a3: Real text pulls reviewers into the content, while placeholder text lets them judge fonts, spacing and layout more objectively.
lorem-ipsum.faq.q4: Can it produce an exact number of words?
lorem-ipsum.faq.a4: Yes. Choose the Words unit and the tool returns exactly the number of words you ask for.
lorem-ipsum.faq.q5: Should I remember to replace the placeholder text before publishing?
lorem-ipsum.faq.a5: Yes. Review the whole page before publishing so no Lorem Ipsum paragraph slips through.

regex-tester.pattern: Pattern (no need for / at both ends)
regex-tester.sample: Contact: support@websitefreetools.com or sales@example.com, phone +1 (555) 123-4567. Deadline 12/15/2026. Website https://websitefreetools.com
regex-tester.replaceWith: Replace with ($1, $2… are groups, $& is the whole match)
regex-tester.c.anchor: Any character, start of line, end of line
regex-tester.c.quant: 0 or more, 1 or more, optional, 2 to 5 times
regex-tester.c.set: One of the characters, none of the characters, character range
regex-tester.c.group: Numbered group, non-capturing group, named group
regex-tester.c.alt: Or, word boundary, positive lookahead, negative lookahead
regex-tester.seo.howTitle: How to test a regular expression
regex-tester.seo.how1: Enter your pattern in the top box (no need for / at both ends) and the test text below. Matches are highlighted, and the table below lists each result, its position and the values of the ( ) groups.
regex-tester.seo.how2: Turn on flags such as g (find all), i (case-insensitive), m (per line), s (dot matches line breaks) and u (Unicode, needed for accented letters).
regex-tester.seo.how3: The Replace section shows the text after replacement, using $1, $2 for groups and $& for the whole match. The tool uses the JavaScript Regex engine.
regex-tester.faq.q1: Which language's regex flavor is this?
regex-tester.faq.a1: JavaScript (ECMAScript) syntax, which is close to PCRE in PHP and Python, with minor differences in lookbehind and some flags.
regex-tester.faq.q2: How do I match accented letters?
regex-tester.faq.a2: Turn on the u flag and use \p{L} to match any letter in any language, including accented ones.
regex-tester.faq.q3: What is the standard email regex?
regex-tester.faq.a3: There is no perfect pattern. The built-in preset is enough for basic checks, but for real validation you should send a confirmation email.
regex-tester.faq.q4: Why does the page slow down with some patterns?
regex-tester.faq.a4: Patterns with nested repetition such as (a+)+ can take a very long time to run. Write a more specific pattern.
regex-tester.faq.a5: No. Everything stays on the page until you close it.

json-to-types.note: Fields that appear in only some array items are marked optional, and null values make that field nullable. Integers and floating-point numbers are distinguished when the target language has both types.
json-to-types.seo.howTitle: How the tool infers data types
json-to-types.seo.how1: The tool reads each value in the JSON: string, integer, float, boolean, array and nested object, then creates a separate type for every child object, named after the field.
json-to-types.seo.how2: For arrays with many items, the objects are merged: fields present in only some items are marked optional, and fields with null values are marked nullable.
json-to-types.seo.how3: The output is a good starting point. You should review type names, date types (which are left as strings) and fields that can hold multiple types.
json-to-types.faq.q1: Does it support very large JSON?
json-to-types.faq.a1: Yes, but a representative sample is all you need. JSON of a few MB still runs fine on a computer.
json-to-types.faq.q2: Why is a date field a string?
json-to-types.faq.a2: JSON has no date type, so dates are always strings. You can change them to Date or time.Time afterward.
json-to-types.faq.q3: What is a Zod schema for?
json-to-types.faq.a3: Zod validates data at runtime (for example API responses) and infers the TypeScript type from the same definition.
json-to-types.faq.q4: How are field names with spaces handled?
json-to-types.faq.a4: TypeScript puts the name in quotes. Go and C# convert it to PascalCase and keep the original name in the json tag.
json-to-types.faq.q5: What type is an empty array?
json-to-types.faq.a5: An empty array doesn't give enough information, so the element type is unknown/any. Add a sample element.

json-viewer.treeHint: Click a row to see its JSONPath.
json-viewer.seo.howTitle: How to read and query JSON
json-viewer.seo.how1: Paste JSON into the left box and the tree on the right shows each object and array with its item count. Click the arrows to expand or collapse, and click a row to get its JSONPath.
json-viewer.seo.how2: JSONPath is like an address for data: $ is the root, .name is a field, [0] is the first item, [*] is every item, .. searches at any depth, and [?(@.price<35)] filters by a condition.
json-viewer.seo.how3: The Pretty-print button indents the JSON, and the Sort keys A-Z button makes it easier to compare two JSON documents.
json-viewer.faq.a1: The idea is the same: write a path to select data. JSONPath is for JSON, while XPath is for XML.
json-viewer.faq.a2: Comparisons ==, !=, >, <, >=, <= with numbers or strings, and checking that a field exists with [?(@.name)].
json-viewer.faq.q3: Where does the JSON error point?
json-viewer.faq.a3: The error message includes the position of the bad character. Common causes are a trailing comma or single quotes instead of double quotes.
json-viewer.faq.a4: No. The JSON is processed entirely in your browser.
json-viewer.faq.q5: Can I open very large JSON files?
json-viewer.faq.a5: A few MB is fine, but files of tens of MB may make the tree slow to display.

yaml-json-toml.note: TOML can only hold a table (object) at the top level and has no null values. Data that doesn't fit will show an error with the reason. Comments (#) are not preserved when converting.
yaml-json-toml.tomlRoot: TOML requires the root data to be an object (table), not an array or a single value.
yaml-json-toml.seo.how1: JSON is strict and widely used in APIs. YAML is easy to read thanks to indentation and is popular in Docker Compose, Kubernetes and GitHub Actions. TOML is explicit and table-based, used by Cargo (Rust), pyproject (Python) and Hugo.
yaml-json-toml.seo.how2: Choose the source and target formats and the result updates as you type. The Swap direction button moves the result into the input so you can convert back.
yaml-json-toml.seo.how3: TOML has no null value and requires a table at the root, so null fields are dropped when converting to TOML. Comments in YAML/TOML are not preserved.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q1: What does a YAML indentation error mean?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a1: YAML uses spaces to show nesting. Tabs are not allowed, and items at the same level must line up.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q2: Is data lost when converting YAML to JSON?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a2: No data is lost. Only comments are dropped, and anchors (&, *) are expanded into concrete values.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q3: Why does yes/no in YAML become true/false?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a3: The library follows the YAML 1.2 standard, so yes/no stay as strings. Only true/false are booleans.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q4: Do I need an internet connection to run it?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a4: The first time, the tool loads the js-yaml and smol-toml libraries from a CDN. After that, everything is processed on your device.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q5: Are TOML dates and times preserved?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a5: TOML dates and times are converted to ISO strings when converting to JSON/YAML.

sql-format.note: Supports common SQL syntax for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and SQLite: SELECT, JOIN, subqueries, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. Quoted content and comments are preserved.
sql-format.seo.how1: SQL written on a single line or generated by software is very hard to read. The tool puts each clause (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY) on its own line, with each column and each AND/OR condition on a separate line.
sql-format.seo.how2: Subqueries in parentheses are indented one extra level, and JOIN types start their own lines. Quoted strings and comments are preserved.
sql-format.seo.how3: The Minify to one line button removes comments and extra whitespace, which is handy for pasting into source code or logs.
sql-format.faq.q1: Does formatting change the query result?
sql-format.faq.a1: No. Only whitespace and the letter case of keywords change. Table names, column names and values stay the same.
sql-format.faq.a2: The tool handles common SQL syntax. Vendor-specific statements (stored procedures, PL/SQL) still get basic line breaks.
sql-format.faq.a3: It's not required, but it is a common convention that helps distinguish keywords from table and column names.
sql-format.faq.q4: Does it check SQL syntax errors?
sql-format.faq.a4: No. The tool only formats. Run the query against your database to check for errors.
sql-format.faq.q5: Is the data in my statement sent anywhere?
sql-format.faq.a5: No. Formatting happens in your browser.
