markdown-html.note: HTML in the preview is sanitized to remove scripts and dangerous attributes for safety.
markdown-html.seo.how1: Markdown is a way to write formatted text using simple symbols: # for headings, **text** for bold and - for lists. It is used on GitHub, Notion, Reddit, many blogs and technical documentation.
markdown-html.seo.how2: Type Markdown on the left and the preview appears instantly. The box below holds the HTML code to paste into a website or email. GitHub style adds support for tables, strikethrough and natural line breaks.
markdown-html.seo.how3: The HTML to Markdown tab converts articles and old web pages to Markdown so you can move them into a new system.
markdown-html.faq.q1: Does it support tables in Markdown?
markdown-html.faq.a1: Yes. Use | to separate columns and a |---| line under the header, as in the built-in sample.
markdown-html.faq.q2: Is the exported HTML safe to paste into a website?
markdown-html.faq.a2: The preview is sanitized to remove scripts, but the exported code keeps exactly what you wrote, so review it if the content comes from someone else.
markdown-html.faq.q3: Does HTML to Markdown keep images?
markdown-html.faq.a3: Yes. tags are converted to the ![description](path) syntax.
markdown-html.faq.q4: Do I need an internet connection?
markdown-html.faq.a4: The first time, the tool loads the marked, DOMPurify and Turndown libraries from a CDN. After that it runs on your device.
markdown-html.faq.a5: Yes: CommonMark, GitHub Flavored Markdown and others. The tool follows the GitHub standard, the most common one.

cron-gen.expr: Cron expression (minute hour day month weekday)
cron-gen.never: This expression never runs (for example, February 31).
cron-gen.bad: Invalid expression. It needs 5 parts separated by spaces: minute (0-59) hour (0-23) day (1-31) month (1-12) weekday (0-6, 0 = Sunday). Use * , - / such as */5 or 1-5.
cron-gen.seo.how1: A cron expression has 5 parts separated by spaces: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12) and day of week (0-6, where 0 is Sunday). An asterisk * means every value.
cron-gen.seo.how2: Use commas for lists (1,15), hyphens for ranges (1-5) and a slash for steps (*/15 means every 15 minutes). You can also use English abbreviations such as MON-FRI and JAN.
cron-gen.seo.how3: The tool calculates the next 10 runs so you can be sure the schedule is right before putting it into crontab, GitHub Actions, a Kubernetes CronJob or a service scheduler.
cron-gen.faq.q1: Which time zone does cron use?
cron-gen.faq.a1: The time zone of the server running cron. GitHub Actions uses UTC, so 9 AM Eastern Standard Time (UTC-5) is 0 14 * * *.
cron-gen.faq.q2: What if I set both day of month and day of week?
cron-gen.faq.a2: Under the Unix cron rule, the job runs when either condition matches, not both.
cron-gen.faq.q3: How do I run a job every 30 seconds?
cron-gen.faq.a3: Standard cron has a minimum of 1 minute. For 30 seconds you need two entries, with the second one using sleep 30.
cron-gen.faq.q5: Does it support 6-field cron with seconds?
cron-gen.faq.a5: The tool uses standard Unix 5-field cron. Quartz and Spring add a seconds field at the start.

number-base.note: Type in any box and the others convert automatically. Supports very large numbers (unlimited digits), negative numbers and the prefixes 0x, 0b, 0o. You can use _ or spaces to group digits.
number-base.overflow: The value is outside the {b}-bit range.
number-base.bad: Contains a digit that is invalid for base {b}. For example, binary only has 0 and 1, and hex has 0-9 and A-F.
number-base.seo.how1: Computers store everything as binary numbers (0 and 1). Hexadecimal (hex) is more compact, with each digit equal to 4 bits, so it is widely used for color codes, memory addresses and hashes.
number-base.seo.how2: Type in any box and the others update instantly. The tool uses BigInt integers, so there is no limit on the number of digits, and it accepts the prefixes 0x, 0b and 0o.
number-base.seo.how3: Two's complement shows how computers store negative numbers in 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits, which is useful when learning embedded programming and assembly.
number-base.faq.q1: How do I convert decimal to binary by hand?
number-base.faq.a1: Keep dividing the number by 2 and write down the remainders, then read the remainders from bottom to top.
number-base.faq.q2: Why does hex use the letters A-F?
number-base.faq.a2: Base 16 needs 16 digits. After 0-9, the letters A-F represent 10 to 15.
number-base.faq.a3: It is a way to store negative numbers: invert every bit of the positive number and add 1. For example, -1 in 8 bits is 11111111.
number-base.faq.a4: Not yet. The tool only converts integers.
number-base.faq.a5: It is used to shorten numbers into short strings, such as short link codes and order numbers.

curl-convert.note: Understands common options: -X, -H, -d / --data / --data-raw / --json, --data-urlencode, -F, -u, -A, -b, -e. Tip: in your browser's Network tab, right-click a request → Copy → Copy as cURL, then paste it here.
curl-convert.noCurl: The command must start with the word curl.
curl-convert.noUrl: No URL was found in the command.
curl-convert.quote: The command has an unclosed quote. Check for a missing ' or ".
curl-convert.seo.howTitle: How to convert cURL to code
curl-convert.seo.how1: cURL is a command for sending HTTP requests that is common in API documentation. The tool reads the method, URL, headers (-H), body (-d, --json), form data (-F) and credentials (-u), then rewrites them in the language you choose.
curl-convert.seo.how2: JSON bodies are recognized and written as clean objects (JSON.stringify, json= in Python). The -u credentials are converted into a Basic Authorization header.
curl-convert.seo.how3: Tip: open developer tools (F12) → Network, right-click a request → Copy → Copy as cURL (bash), then paste it here to recreate that exact request.
curl-convert.faq.q1: Does it support multi-line cURL commands with \?
curl-convert.faq.a1: Yes. A \ at the end of a line is joined automatically.
curl-convert.faq.q2: Does Copy as cURL from Windows (cmd) work?
curl-convert.faq.a2: Choose the bash version. The cmd version uses ^ for escaping, so it may be misread.
curl-convert.faq.q3: Is the token in my command sent anywhere?
curl-convert.faq.a3: No. The conversion runs in your browser. Even so, don't share code that contains a real token.
curl-convert.faq.q4: Calling an API with fetch from the browser gives a CORS error. Why?
curl-convert.faq.a4: That is a limit set by the API server, not a bug in the code. Call it from a server (Node.js) or enable CORS on the API side.
curl-convert.faq.a5: Display and network options such as -o, -w, --max-time and -x have no effect in code, so they are ignored.

json-diff.same: The two JSON documents have identical content.
json-diff.seo.how1: A plain text comparison reports differences just because keys were reordered or whitespace changed. This tool parses the JSON into data and compares key by key, so it only reports real differences in content.
json-diff.seo.how2: Each difference has a path such as $.settings.theme, the type of change (added, removed, value changed, type changed) and the values on both sides, color-coded for readability.
json-diff.seo.how3: Turn on Ignore array item order when arrays are just sets (lists of tags or permissions) so that sorting differences are not reported.
json-diff.faq.q1: Are different key orders treated as a difference?
json-diff.faq.a1: No. Two objects with the same keys and values are considered identical even if the order is different.
json-diff.faq.q2: Are the number 1 and the string 1 different?
json-diff.faq.a2: Yes, that is reported as a type change.
json-diff.faq.q3: What is it used for in practice?
json-diff.faq.a3: Comparing API responses between two versions, config files between test and production environments, and data before and after processing.
json-diff.faq.a4: Yes. The Copy report button gives a table-style list you can paste into Excel or a message.
json-diff.faq.a5: JSON of a few MB is fine. Very long arrays with the ignore-order option will be slower.

fake-data.f.name: Full name
fake-data.note: The data is randomly generated and is for software testing, interface mockups and trial database imports only. Any resemblance to real people is coincidental.
fake-data.seo.how1: When developing software, you need realistic-looking data to test interfaces, pagination, search and file import/export without using real customer information.
fake-data.seo.how2: Choose a country to get names, phone numbers, cities and email domains in that country's style, then pick the fields you need and the number of rows (up to 5,000).
fake-data.seo.how3: Export JSON for a mock API, CSV or a table to open in Excel, or SQL INSERT statements to load straight into a test database.
fake-data.faq.q1: Is the data about real people?
fake-data.faq.a1: No. Names and phone numbers are randomly assembled from common lists. Any match with a real person is coincidental.
fake-data.faq.q2: Can fake emails actually receive mail?
fake-data.faq.a2: The domains are gmail.com, outlook.com and so on, so don't send real emails to these addresses. Use them for local testing only.
fake-data.faq.q3: My CSV file shows garbled characters in Excel. Why?
fake-data.faq.a3: The tool adds a UTF-8 BOM when you download CSV so Excel displays accented characters correctly.
fake-data.faq.q4: Can I generate more than 5,000 rows?
fake-data.faq.a4: The limit keeps your browser from freezing. Generate several batches and combine them if you need more.
fake-data.faq.q5: Can I use it for load-testing data?
fake-data.faq.a5: Yes, but for millions of rows use a library such as Faker on a server.

gitignore-gen.note: Place the .gitignore file in your project root. Files Git was already tracking are not ignored automatically: run git rm --cached file-name to untrack them.
gitignore-gen.seo.how1: A .gitignore file lists the files and folders Git should not track: downloaded libraries (node_modules), build output, config files that contain passwords (.env), and junk files from operating systems and editors.
gitignore-gen.seo.how2: Pick the entries that match your project and the tool merges them into one file with a heading for each section. You can add your own lines in the last box.
gitignore-gen.seo.how3: Download the file and put it in your project root with exactly the name .gitignore (a leading dot, no extension).
gitignore-gen.faq.q1: I added a file to .gitignore but it is still tracked. Why?
gitignore-gen.faq.a1: A file that was committed earlier is still tracked. Run git rm --cached file-name and commit again.
gitignore-gen.faq.q2: Should I commit the .env file to Git?
gitignore-gen.faq.a2: No. Add it to .gitignore and create a .env.example file with no real values so others know which variables are needed.
gitignore-gen.faq.a3: It is an exception: files matching that pattern are not ignored, even if an earlier line ignored the whole folder.
gitignore-gen.faq.q4: Windows won't let me name a file .gitignore. What do I do?
gitignore-gen.faq.a4: Save the file as .gitignore. (with a trailing dot) or create it in VS Code, and Windows will remove the trailing dot automatically.
gitignore-gen.faq.q5: Are the templates taken from GitHub?
gitignore-gen.faq.a5: The templates are compactly written by WFTools, following the common conventions of each technology.

meta-tags.title: Page title
meta-tags.s.title: Free Online Tools — WFTools
meta-tags.s.desc: Over 200 free online tools: make QR codes, compress images, merge PDFs, convert units. Runs right in your browser with nothing to install.
meta-tags.code: Code to paste into the <head> tag
meta-tags.tLen: {n} characters — aim for 30 to 60 so Google doesn't truncate it.
meta-tags.seo.how1: The title tag and meta description are the first things people see on Google. A title should be 30 to 60 characters and contain your main keyword; a description of 110 to 160 characters should be compelling to improve click-through rate.
meta-tags.seo.how2: Open Graph (og:) tags determine the title, description and image when a link is shared on Facebook or LinkedIn. The image should be 1200×630 px.
meta-tags.seo.how3: The canonical tag tells Google which address is the main one for a page to avoid duplicates; robots allows or blocks Google from indexing.
meta-tags.faq.q1: Will adding meta tags get me to the top of Google?
meta-tags.faq.a1: Title and description are not the only factor, but they strongly affect click-through rate, which indirectly helps rankings.
meta-tags.faq.q2: Why doesn't Facebook show my new image when I share?
meta-tags.faq.a2: Facebook caches the old tags. Use Facebook's Sharing Debugger tool to refresh them.
meta-tags.faq.q3: Does the meta keywords tag still matter?
meta-tags.faq.a3: No. Google ignored the keywords tag long ago, so this tool doesn't generate it.
meta-tags.faq.q4: Where do I paste the code?
meta-tags.faq.a4: Paste it into the <head> section of your page, replacing any old title and description tags.
meta-tags.faq.q5: Do I need separate tags for LinkedIn?
meta-tags.faq.a5: No. LinkedIn reads Open Graph tags just like Facebook.

browser-info.ipNote: Your IP address is only looked up when you click the button, using the free service api.ipify.org.
browser-info.ipFail: Could not look up the IP address (network error or an ad blocker is blocking the service). Try turning off the blocker and click again.
browser-info.seo.how1: When reporting a website bug or asking for tech support, you are often asked which browser, which version and what screen size you use. This page gathers it all, ready to copy with one click.
browser-info.seo.how2: The User-Agent string is how your browser introduces itself to every website. The viewport and pixel ratio (DPR) help developers test layouts on phones.
browser-info.seo.how3: The public IP address is only looked up when you click the button, using the free service api.ipify.org. Everything else is read directly from your browser and never sent anywhere.
browser-info.faq.q1: Is this IP address the IP of my computer?
browser-info.faq.a1: It is the public IP of your network (modem, internet provider). Devices on your local network have different private IPs, like 192.168.x.x.
browser-info.faq.q2: Why does Windows 11 show as Windows 10/11?
browser-info.faq.a2: Browsers report the same identifier for Windows 10 and 11, so they can't be told apart from the User-Agent.
browser-info.faq.q3: Why does it show less RAM than my computer has?
browser-info.faq.a3: Browsers report a rounded number capped at 8 GB to protect your privacy.
browser-info.faq.a4: Yes. Any website you open can read most of this information.
browser-info.faq.q5: What IP is shown if I use a VPN?
browser-info.faq.a5: It shows the IP of the VPN server, not your real IP.

favicon-gen.pick: Choose a square image (PNG, SVG, JPG; 512×512 or larger recommended)
favicon-gen.noImg: Please choose an image first, or switch to the "From text or emoji" tab.
favicon-gen.seo.how1: A favicon is the small icon on browser tabs and bookmarks. Besides favicon.ico, phones need a 180 px image for the iPhone home screen and 192 and 512 px images for Android and web apps (PWA).
favicon-gen.seo.how2: Choose a square image (ideally a transparent PNG or an SVG, 512×512 px or larger) or type a letter or emoji and pick colors. The tool redraws it at every required size.
favicon-gen.seo.how3: The ZIP contains favicon.ico (16, 32, 48 px), the PNG files, site.webmanifest and head.html with the code to insert in the <head> tag.
favicon-gen.faq.q1: Where do I put the favicon files?
favicon-gen.faq.a1: Put them in your website root (next to index.html), then paste the code from head.html into the <head> tag.
favicon-gen.faq.q2: I changed my favicon but the browser still shows the old one. Why?
favicon-gen.faq.a2: Browsers cache favicons for a very long time. Clear the cache or open a private tab to check.
favicon-gen.faq.q3: Do I need an SVG favicon?
favicon-gen.faq.a3: Not required. The PNG and ICO set is enough for every browser.
favicon-gen.faq.a4: The image is centered in a square and keeps its proportions. Use the icon part of your logo rather than long text.
favicon-gen.faq.a5: No. The image is redrawn right in your browser.

css-generator.seo.how1: A box-shadow has a horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur, spread and color. Soft, attractive shadows usually have a large blur, a negative spread and low opacity (10 to 25%).
css-generator.seo.how2: A gradient creates a color-blended background: linear along an angle, radial from the center, or conic around a center point. Add a third color for a richer blend.
css-generator.seo.how3: Frosted glass (glassmorphism) uses a translucent background, backdrop-filter to blur what is behind it and a thin light border. It looks best over a colorful background.
css-generator.faq.q1: Does backdrop-filter work in every browser?
css-generator.faq.a1: It works in recent versions of Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox. The code includes the -webkit- prefix for older Safari.
css-generator.faq.q2: How do I make a multi-layer shadow?
css-generator.faq.a2: Separate shadows with commas inside the same box-shadow. Create each layer, then combine them.
css-generator.faq.q3: Can I replace px units with rem?
css-generator.faq.a3: Yes. Divide the px value by 16 to get rem if the root font size is 16 px.
css-generator.faq.q4: How do I make a perfect circle?
css-generator.faq.a4: Set the radius to half the width, or use border-radius: 50% on a square element.
css-generator.faq.q5: Do gradients make a page heavy?
css-generator.faq.a5: No. Gradients are drawn by the browser and are much lighter than background images.

flex-grid.note: Change the options and see right away how the items are arranged. Click a cell to make it bigger (flex-grow or spanning 2 columns).
flex-grid.seo.how1: Flexbox arranges items in one direction (row or column), which suits menu bars, button groups and centering. Grid arranges in two dimensions, rows and columns at once, which suits page layouts and product grids.
flex-grid.seo.how2: Change each property and watch the preview to understand its effect: justify-content aligns along the main axis, align-items along the cross axis, and gap is the spacing between items.
flex-grid.seo.how3: Click a cell to make it larger (flex-grow in Flexbox, spanning 2 columns in Grid). The CSS code updates to match so you can paste it into your project.
flex-grid.faq.q1: How do I center an element?
flex-grid.faq.a1: Set display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center on the container.
flex-grid.faq.a2: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(120px, 1fr)) calculates the number of columns from the screen width, which is great for responsive product grids.
flex-grid.faq.a3: fr is a fraction of the free space. 1fr 2fr means the second column is twice as wide as the first.
flex-grid.faq.a4: Yes. All modern browsers support gap for Flexbox.
flex-grid.faq.q5: Should I use Flexbox or Grid?
flex-grid.faq.a5: Often both: Grid for the page frame and Flexbox for the content inside each cell.

svg-optimize.pick: Choose an SVG file or paste code below
svg-optimize.o.ed: Remove Inkscape, Illustrator and Figma data
svg-optimize.bad: Could not read the SVG. Check that the code starts with an <svg> tag and that all tags are properly closed.
svg-optimize.seo.how1: SVG files exported from Inkscape, Illustrator and Figma often contain a lot of software-specific data, comments and long decimals. Removing them can cut the file size by 30 to 70%.
svg-optimize.seo.how2: The tool rounds coordinates to the number of decimal places you choose (2 is enough for icons), shortens paths, and removes empty groups and extra whitespace.
svg-optimize.seo.how3: Compare the image before and after right below. If the image looks off, increase the decimal places to 3.
svg-optimize.faq.a1: No. SVG is a vector image, and sensible rounding is not visible to the eye.
svg-optimize.faq.a2: The image then scales with its container on the web, keeping only the viewBox to preserve proportions.
svg-optimize.faq.q3: Where is a data URI used?
svg-optimize.faq.a3: Paste it straight into CSS background-image or an tag without needing a separate file.
svg-optimize.faq.q4: Does it support SVGs with embedded images?
svg-optimize.faq.a4: Yes, embedded images are kept as they are. For a lighter file, compress that image separately.
svg-optimize.faq.a5: No. WFTools has its own lightweight optimizer that runs in the browser.

url-parser.bad: Could not read the URL. Check that the domain contains a dot and has no spaces.
url-parser.seo.how1: A URL consists of a protocol (https), a domain (shop.example.com), a port, a path (/products/qr), a query string after the ? made of name=value pairs, and an anchor after the #.
url-parser.seo.how2: The parameter table shows decoded values (accented letters, spaces) for readability. Edit directly in the table and the new URL is rebuilt and properly encoded.
url-parser.seo.how3: The Remove tracking parameters button strips utm_source, fbclid, gclid and similar codes that are added when you click links from ads or Facebook, making links shorter and more private to share.
url-parser.faq.q1: Does removing utm break the link?
url-parser.faq.a1: No. Tracking parameters are only for analytics, and the page still opens normally.
url-parser.faq.a2: It is a code Facebook appends to links when you click from Facebook, used to measure ads.
url-parser.faq.q3: Why is the password in the URL hidden?
url-parser.faq.a3: To avoid exposing it in screenshots. You should never put a password in a link.
url-parser.faq.a4: The tool only tidies up parameters. Making a short link requires a service with a server.
url-parser.faq.q5: Is it OK to leave out https://?
url-parser.faq.a5: Yes. The tool adds https:// automatically when the link has no protocol.

subnet-calc.ip4: IP address and prefix (CIDR) or subnet mask
subnet-calc.splitSmall: Choose a prefix larger than /{p} to split.
subnet-calc.bad4: Invalid address. Valid examples: 192.168.1.10/24 or 10.0.0.1 255.255.0.0 (each part from 0 to 255, prefix from 0 to 32).
subnet-calc.bad6: Invalid IPv6 address. Example: 2001:db8::1/64 (8 hex groups, use :: once to replace a run of zeros).
subnet-calc.seo.how1: A /24 prefix means the first 24 bits of the address are the network part and the remaining 8 bits are for hosts, equal to the subnet mask 255.255.255.0 and 254 usable hosts.
subnet-calc.seo.how2: The network address (all host bits 0) and the broadcast address (all host bits 1) are not assigned to devices, so usable hosts equal total addresses minus 2 (except for /31 and /32).
subnet-calc.seo.how3: Choose a larger prefix in the Split section to list the subnets, for example splitting a /24 into sixteen /28 networks for individual departments.
subnet-calc.faq.q1: What prefix is the subnet mask 255.255.255.0?
subnet-calc.faq.a1: It is /24. Each 255 equals 8 one-bits, so three 255s make 24 bits.
subnet-calc.faq.q2: Where is a wildcard mask used?
subnet-calc.faq.a2: In ACLs and OSPF on Cisco devices. It is the inverse of the subnet mask.
subnet-calc.faq.a4: The IPv6 standard specifies /64 for LANs so devices can configure their own addresses (SLAAC).
subnet-calc.faq.q5: How do I shorten an IPv6 address?
subnet-calc.faq.a5: Drop leading zeros in each group and replace the longest run of consecutive zero groups with ::, using :: only once.

robots-sitemap.dis: Folders to block from crawling (one path per line)
robots-sitemap.urls: Page list (one path or full URL per line)
robots-sitemap.hRobots: Place the file at your domain root: https://your-domain.com/robots.txt. robots.txt is only a request, not a security measure.
robots-sitemap.hSitemap: Upload the file to your domain root, then submit it in Google Search Console and reference it in robots.txt. A sitemap can hold up to 50,000 URLs.
robots-sitemap.seo.how1: robots.txt sits at the root of your domain and tells search bots which folders not to crawl (admin pages, carts, internal search results) and where the sitemap is.
robots-sitemap.seo.how2: You can block bots that collect data to train AI, such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and CCBot, while still letting Google index your site normally.
robots-sitemap.seo.how3: sitemap.xml lists your important pages so Google finds them faster. Paste a list of paths and the tool adds the domain, last-modified date and a priority based on depth.
robots-sitemap.faq.a1: No. It is only a request to bots, and the page can still be opened. To truly block access you need a password or noindex.
robots-sitemap.faq.q2: Will blocking with robots.txt remove a page from Google?
robots-sitemap.faq.a2: Not necessarily. Google may still show the address if other pages link to it. Use a noindex meta tag to remove it from results.
robots-sitemap.faq.q3: How many links can a sitemap hold?
robots-sitemap.faq.a3: 50,000 URLs or 50 MB per file. Larger sites split into several sitemaps plus a sitemap index.
robots-sitemap.faq.a4: Google almost completely ignores these two tags. An accurate lastmod is what helps.
robots-sitemap.faq.q5: Where do I submit a sitemap to Google?
robots-sitemap.faq.a5: In Google Search Console under Sitemaps, and with a Sitemap: line in robots.txt.

http-status.c100: The server received the request headers; the client should continue sending the body.
http-status.c101: Switching to another protocol, for example upgrading to WebSocket.
http-status.c200: Success; the response contains the requested data.
http-status.c201: A new resource was created (usually after a POST).
http-status.c202: The request was accepted and will be processed later (not finished yet).
http-status.c204: Success, but there is no content to return.
http-status.c206: Part of a file was returned (resumed downloads, video seeking).
http-status.c301: The page has moved permanently to a new address; Google passes SEO value to the new address.
http-status.c302: Temporary redirect; the old address stays in search results.
http-status.c303: See the result at another address using GET (after submitting a form).
http-status.c304: Content is unchanged; the browser uses its cached copy.
http-status.c307: Temporary redirect that keeps the method (a POST stays a POST).
http-status.c308: Permanent redirect that keeps the method.
http-status.c400: The request has bad syntax or is missing required data.
http-status.c401: Not signed in, or the token has expired.
http-status.c402: Payment required (rarely used; some APIs report an exhausted quota).
http-status.c403: Recognized, but you have no permission to access this.
http-status.c404: The page or resource was not found.
http-status.c405: The method (GET, POST…) is not supported at this address.
http-status.c406: No response format matches the Accept request header.
http-status.c408: The client sent the request too slowly, so the server stopped waiting.
http-status.c409: Data conflict, such as a duplicate name or an outdated version.
http-status.c410: The resource has been permanently deleted.
http-status.c413: The uploaded data is too large (the file exceeds the limit).
http-status.c415: The format of the uploaded data is not supported.
http-status.c418: A joke code in the standard: the server is a teapot and does not brew coffee.
http-status.c422: Correct syntax but invalid data (form validation error).
http-status.c425: The server is unwilling to process a request that might be replayed.
http-status.c428: A condition header (If-Match) is required to prevent overwriting.
http-status.c429: Too many requests, so you are rate-limited; try again later.
http-status.c431: The request headers are too large (often because of too many cookies).
http-status.c500: A general server-side error (code bug, misconfiguration).
http-status.c501: The server does not support this feature.
http-status.c502: A gateway server received an error response from the upstream server.
http-status.c503: The server is overloaded or down for maintenance.
http-status.c504: A gateway server waited too long for the upstream server.
http-status.c505: The HTTP version is not supported.
http-status.c507: The server has run out of storage space.
http-status.c511: Network login required (coffee shop or hotel Wi-Fi).
http-status.msearch: Search by file extension or MIME type
http-status.seo.how1: Every time a browser calls a server, the server returns a 3-digit code. The 2xx group means success, 3xx means redirection, 4xx means a problem with the request (wrong address, not signed in) and 5xx means a server error.
http-status.seo.how2: For SEO, use 301 when a page address changes permanently to keep rankings, and 404 or 410 for deleted pages. Avoid returning 200 on error pages.
http-status.seo.how3: The MIME types tab shows the correct Content-Type for each file extension, which you need when configuring servers, uploading files or calling APIs.
http-status.faq.a1: A few 404 pages are normal. Only add 301 redirects for old pages that get a lot of traffic or have many links pointing to them.
http-status.faq.q2: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
http-status.faq.a2: 401 means not signed in or the session expired; 403 means you are signed in but have no permission.
http-status.faq.a3: An intermediary server (Nginx, Cloudflare) did not get a valid response (502) or waited too long (504) from the application server behind it.
http-status.faq.q4: How do I handle 429 Too Many Requests?
http-status.faq.a4: You sent too many requests in a short time. Wait a while or reduce how often you call the API.
http-status.faq.q5: When should I use 302 instead of 301?
http-status.faq.a5: For temporary redirects, such as a maintenance page or a short-term promotion.

contrast-check.demoText: Sample paragraph to check whether the text is easy to read on this background. Older people and people with low vision need high contrast.
contrast-check.note: Under WCAG 2.1: level AA needs a minimum ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; level AAA needs 7:1 and 4.5:1. UI components (input borders, icons) need 3:1.
contrast-check.seo.how1: Light text on a light background is hard to read for older people, people with low vision, and phone users in bright sunlight. WCAG sets minimum ratios so that everyone can read your content.
contrast-check.seo.how2: Ratios range from 1:1 (the same color) to 21:1 (black on white). Level AA needs 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; level AAA needs 7:1 and 4.5:1.
contrast-check.seo.how3: Click Suggest an AA-compliant text color and the tool darkens or lightens your text color just enough while keeping your brand hue.
contrast-check.faq.a1: 24 px and up, or roughly 18.5 px and up if bold.
contrast-check.faq.q2: Does a logo need to pass?
contrast-check.faq.a2: No. WCAG exempts logos and decorative text, but text that carries content should pass.
contrast-check.faq.a3: Many countries require government and bank websites to meet AA. For ordinary websites it is a recommended level.
contrast-check.faq.q4: How do I check contrast for text over an image?
contrast-check.faq.a4: Take the color from the lightest area of the image behind the text, or add a dark overlay to guarantee enough contrast.
contrast-check.faq.q5: Does the tool handle semi-transparent colors?
contrast-check.faq.a5: Not yet. Use a solid color after blending it with the background.

embed-code.url: YouTube, Vimeo, Google Maps, Google Drive/Docs link or any web page
embed-code.title: Title (for screen readers)
embed-code.s.title: Intro video
embed-code.lazy: Lazy loading so the page opens faster
embed-code.web: Web page (some sites don't allow embedding)
embed-code.bad: Invalid link. Please paste the full address starting with https://
embed-code.seo.howTitle: Embedding videos and maps the right way
embed-code.seo.how1: YouTube's default embed code has a fixed width, so it overflows on phones. The tool wraps the iframe in a container that keeps a 16:9 ratio (or 9:16 for Shorts) and resizes with the screen.
embed-code.seo.how2: Just paste a normal link (including links with &t=30s) and the tool converts it to the proper embed link, adding the start time, autoplay and loop as you choose.
embed-code.seo.how3: Lazy loading (loading=lazy) makes the page open faster because the video only loads when the viewer scrolls to it. YouTube no-cookie mode limits viewer tracking.
embed-code.faq.a1: Browsers only allow autoplay when muted, so the tool adds mute automatically when you turn on autoplay.
embed-code.faq.q2: Can I embed a private video?
embed-code.faq.a2: No. The video must be public or unlisted, and the owner must allow embedding.
embed-code.faq.q3: How do I embed Google Maps for my location?
embed-code.faq.a3: Paste a place link from Google Maps, or use Google's Share → Embed a map button for the most accurate map.
embed-code.faq.q4: My Google Drive file doesn't show. Why?
embed-code.faq.a4: The file must be shared as Anyone with the link can view.
embed-code.faq.q5: Can I paste it into WordPress or Blogger?
embed-code.faq.a5: Yes. Use a Custom HTML block (WordPress) or HTML view (Blogger) to paste the code.

pdf-pages.noFile: Please choose a PDF file first.
pdf-pages.badRange: Invalid page list. Example: 1, 3-5, 8 (pages must be between 1 and {n}).
pdf-pages.needDel: Enter the page numbers to delete.
pdf-pages.allDel: You can't delete every page. Keep at least one page.
pdf-pages.seo.how1: The Rotate pages tab rotates selected pages by 90°, 180° or 270°, which is useful for upside-down scanned files. Leave the pages box blank to rotate the whole file.
pdf-pages.seo.how2: The Number pages tab adds numbers at the top or bottom of each page in several styles (1, 1 / 10, Page 1 / 10), skips the first cover pages and lets you pick the starting number.
pdf-pages.seo.how3: The Delete pages tab removes unwanted pages; enter a list such as 2, 5-7. To extract pages or merge several files, use the Merge and Split PDF tool.
pdf-pages.faq.a1: No. The file is processed by the pdf-lib library right in your browser.
pdf-pages.faq.q2: Can I choose the page number font?
pdf-pages.faq.a2: Page numbers use the Be Vietnam Pro font, which displays accented letters and many alphabets correctly.
pdf-pages.faq.q3: Can it process a password-protected file?
pdf-pages.faq.a3: No. Unlock the file first with software that accepts the password.
pdf-pages.faq.q4: How do I enter a page list?
pdf-pages.faq.a4: Separate with commas and use a hyphen for consecutive ranges: 1, 3-5, 8.
pdf-pages.faq.a5: No. Rotating only changes the page orientation setting, and the content stays the same.

email-signature.name: Full name
email-signature.s.name: John Smith
email-signature.title: Job title
email-signature.s.title: Sales Manager
email-signature.how: Gmail: Settings → See all settings → Signature → Create new → paste. Outlook: Settings → Mail → Compose and reply → Signature → paste. Images must be public links (https); you can't paste an image from your computer.
email-signature.copied: Copied. Now paste it into your email signature settings
email-signature.seo.howTitle: How to create and install an email signature
email-signature.seo.how1: A professional email signature tells recipients who you are and how to reach you. Fill in your name, job title, company, phone number, email and website, and add a profile photo or logo link if you have one.
email-signature.seo.how2: Choose one of 3 templates (vertical line, card with photo, minimal) and an accent color to match your brand. The signature uses tables and inline styles so it displays reliably in every email app.
email-signature.seo.how3: Click Copy signature and paste it into the signature settings of Gmail or Outlook. The details you enter are remembered in your browser for next time.
email-signature.faq.q1: Why doesn't the image in my signature show?
email-signature.faq.a1: The image must be a public link (https), such as an image on your company website. An image that only exists on your computer won't show on the recipient's device.
email-signature.faq.q2: Does it work with the Outlook desktop app?
email-signature.faq.a2: Yes. Open File → Options → Mail → Signatures, create a new one and paste.
email-signature.faq.q3: What about signatures on a phone?
email-signature.faq.a3: The Gmail phone app only supports plain-text signatures. An HTML signature set up on the web is still used when you send from a computer.
email-signature.faq.q4: Should I use an image of my signature instead of text?
email-signature.faq.a4: Not recommended: images are often blocked, phone numbers can't be tapped and they are hard to read on a phone.
email-signature.faq.q5: Is my information stored on a server?
email-signature.faq.a5: No. Your details are only stored in your browser.

bill-split.round: Round up to a nice number per person
bill-split.gHint: One expense per line: payer name, amount, and (optional) a comma-separated list of people sharing it. Leaving the third part blank means splitting among the whole group.
bill-split.s.exp:
Alex | 120 | 
Brian | 45 | Alex, Brian
Chloe | 30 | 
Dan | 16 | Chloe, Dan
bill-split.copy: Copy result to send to the group
bill-split.badLine: Line {n} is not in the right format: Name | Amount | Shared by
bill-split.seo.how1: The Split a bill evenly tab: enter the total, number of people, tip percentage, tax and discount. The tool works out what each person pays, and can round up to a nice number to make payments easier.
bill-split.seo.how2: The Group expenses tab is for trips and shared parties: each line is one expense with the payer, amount and who shares it. Leaving the sharers blank means splitting among the whole group.
bill-split.seo.how3: The tool calculates each person's balance and then matches debtors with creditors so the number of transfers is as small as possible. Click Copy to send the result to your group chat.
bill-split.faq.q1: What if an expense is shared by only a few people?
bill-split.faq.a1: Write those people's names in the third part, separated by commas, for example: Brian | 45 | Alex, Brian.
bill-split.faq.q2: Is tip calculated on the total before or after tax?
bill-split.faq.a2: The tool calculates both tip and tax on the original bill total before the discount.
bill-split.faq.q3: What happens to leftover money after rounding?
bill-split.faq.a3: The leftover is shown separately so the group knows, and is often used as an extra tip or a shared fund.
bill-split.faq.q4: Are names spelled differently counted as two people?
bill-split.faq.a4: Yes. Write names exactly the same on every line.
bill-split.faq.a5: No. Copy the result before you close the page.

number-words.num: Enter a number (whole number, up to 15 digits)
number-words.c.title: Capitalize Each Word
number-words.vnd: Vietnamese dong amount (for invoices and receipts)
number-words.note: Use this to write amounts in words on invoices, checks, contracts and receipts. Supports negative numbers and very large numbers up to the trillions.
number-words.bad: Enter a whole number below 1 quadrillion.
number-words.seo.howTitle: When you need to write numbers in words
number-words.seo.how1: Invoices, receipts, payment orders, checks and contracts need the amount written in words to prevent tampering with the digits. Enter a number and the tool reads it right away using each language's own rules.
number-words.seo.how2: For Vietnamese, the tool follows the standard conventions of Vietnamese number reading and adds a line with the amount written out in dong at the end, with the first letter capitalized as accounting documents require.
number-words.seo.how3: It supports 20 languages including English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Turkish, Indonesian, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai, Hindi, Bengali and Arabic.
number-words.faq.q1: Is 1,005,000 read with linh or le in Vietnamese?
number-words.faq.a1: The tool uses linh, the form most common on official documents. Some regions say le instead.
number-words.faq.a2: The tool reads the whole-number part. For amounts with cents, write the cents separately.
number-words.faq.q3: What is the largest number it can read?
number-words.faq.a3: Anything below 1 quadrillion (15 digits), enough for any invoice.
number-words.faq.a4: Yes, it adds the word for negative at the start (minus in English, moins in French, and so on).
number-words.faq.q5: Does the English output put and after hundreds?
number-words.faq.a5: The tool reads in American style without inserting and, which suits international checks and invoices.

vietqr.vnNote: The code follows the VietQR standard (NAPAS 247) and can be scanned by the apps of most Vietnamese banks and e-wallets.
vietqr.name: Account holder name (printed on the image, optional)
vietqr.amount: Amount (đ) — leave blank to let the sender enter it
vietqr.check: Scan the code with your own banking app to check that the recipient name is correct before printing it or sending it to customers.
vietqr.privacy: The code is generated on your device. The account number is only saved in this browser so you don't have to retype it next time.
vietqr.memoClean: The memo will be written as: "{m}" (accents and special characters removed so every bank can read it).
vietqr.badAcct: The account number must be digits only, from 6 to 19 digits.
vietqr.seo.how1: VietQR is NAPAS's interbank transfer QR standard, based on the international EMVCo standard. The payer just opens any banking app and scans the code, and the recipient's details are filled in automatically.
vietqr.seo.how2: Choose a bank and enter the account number. Add an amount and memo if you want a code for each order. Leave the amount blank so the sender enters it, which suits a code posted at a counter.
vietqr.seo.how3: The code is generated in your browser without passing through any intermediary server. Download a PNG that includes the bank name, account number and amount to print or send to customers.
vietqr.faq.q1: Can the code be scanned with MoMo or ZaloPay?
vietqr.faq.a1: Yes. Most Vietnamese e-wallets and banking apps can read VietQR codes.
vietqr.faq.q2: Why are accents removed from the transfer memo?
vietqr.faq.a2: Many banks don't accept accented letters or special characters, so the tool converts them to plain letters.
vietqr.faq.q3: Is it safe to share the code?
vietqr.faq.a3: The code only contains the account number (like reading your account number out to someone). Nobody can withdraw money using this code.
vietqr.faq.q4: Is the account holder name inside the code?
vietqr.faq.a4: No. Banking apps look up the real name from the account number. The name you type is only printed on the image.
vietqr.faq.q5: My bank isn't on the list. What now?
vietqr.faq.a5: The list covers over 45 popular banks. Let us know and we will add its BIN code.

qr-scan.pick: Choose an image with a QR code / barcode (or paste one with Ctrl+V)
qr-scan.camNote: Center the code in the frame, hold the device steady and make sure there is enough light. Your browser will ask for camera permission.
qr-scan.safety: Be careful with QR codes posted in public places: check the domain carefully before opening a link or entering passwords or card details.
qr-scan.pay: Payment code (VietQR / EMVCo). Scan it with a banking app to transfer money.
qr-scan.none: No code was found in the image. Try a clearer image, crop closer to the code or shoot it straight on.
qr-scan.camErr: Could not open the camera. Allow the browser to use your camera (lock icon next to the address bar) or use the Scan from image tab.
qr-scan.seo.howTitle: How to scan codes in your browser
qr-scan.seo.how1: The Scan from image tab reads codes in photos, screenshots or images pasted with Ctrl+V, which is handy when someone sends you a QR code in a message and you are using that same phone.
qr-scan.seo.how2: The Scan with camera tab uses your phone's rear camera or a webcam and reads the code automatically when it enters the frame. Your browser asks for camera permission the first time.
qr-scan.seo.how3: The tool recognizes the content: links (showing the domain so you can check before opening), Wi-Fi networks (network name, password) and payment codes.
qr-scan.faq.a1: In Chrome and Edge (Android, macOS) it reads EAN, UPC, Code 128 and more. Other browsers only read QR codes.
qr-scan.faq.q2: Is scanning a QR code dangerous?
qr-scan.faq.a2: A QR code can lead to a scam page. Always check the domain before entering a password or card details.
qr-scan.faq.q3: Why can't it read my code?
qr-scan.faq.a3: The image may be blurry, too small, glared or taken at an angle. Crop closer to the code or retake it straight on with enough light.
qr-scan.faq.a4: No. Images and camera frames are read on your device.
qr-scan.faq.q5: Can I get a Wi-Fi password from a QR code?
qr-scan.faq.a5: Yes. A Wi-Fi QR code contains the network name and password, and the tool displays them clearly so you can enter them manually.

video-frames.bad: Your browser can't play this video (unsupported format or codec). Try converting it to MP4 H.264 with the video trim and convert tool.
video-frames.seo.howTitle: How to get images from a video
video-frames.seo.how1: Choose a video, seek to the moment you need, use the back or forward 1 frame buttons to pick it exactly, then click Capture. The image has the video's original resolution, sharper than a screenshot.
video-frames.seo.how2: Bulk extraction takes one image every number of seconds you choose, which is useful for making thumbnails, grabbing illustrations from tutorial videos or analyzing motion.
video-frames.seo.how3: All images appear in a grid to review. Download them one by one or get the whole set in a single ZIP file.
video-frames.faq.a1: Formats your browser can play: MP4 (H.264), WebM, and MOV on Safari. MKV and AVI videos may need converting first.
video-frames.faq.q2: Can I grab frames from a YouTube video?
video-frames.faq.a2: Not directly. The tool only reads video files on your device.
video-frames.faq.q3: Do the images keep the original quality?
video-frames.faq.a3: Yes, when you choose Original size and the PNG format. JPG is smaller but lightly compressed.
video-frames.faq.a4: No. The video is played and captured right in your browser.
video-frames.faq.q5: How many images can it extract?
video-frames.faq.a5: Up to 500 images at a time so your browser doesn't run out of memory.

image-collage.s.top: WHEN THE CODE WORKS ON THE FIRST TRY
image-collage.hint: Images are cropped to fit the frame automatically (keeping the center). Images follow the order in which you select the files.
image-collage.bad: Some images could not be read and were skipped.
image-collage.seo.howTitle: How to make a photo collage
image-collage.seo.how1: Select several images at once, then choose a layout and frame (square for Instagram, 4:5 portrait, 16:9 landscape, 9:16 story). Images are cropped to fit each cell automatically, keeping the center.
image-collage.seo.how2: Adjust the spacing between cells, the border color and the corner radius to soften the collage. Images follow the order in which you select the files.
image-collage.seo.how3: The meme tab uses the first image and adds text at the top and bottom in the familiar white-with-black-outline style, automatically shrinking the text to fit the image.
image-collage.faq.a1: The collage is exported at the frame size (for example 1080×1080). Download PNG to keep it as sharp as possible.
image-collage.faq.q2: Can I choose which part of each photo shows in the cell?
image-collage.faq.a2: Currently the tool takes the center of the image. Crop the photo first with the Crop Image tool if needed.
image-collage.faq.q3: Can I add text in other languages to a meme?
image-collage.faq.a3: Yes, accented and non-Latin text displays normally.
image-collage.faq.a4: No. The images are combined right in your browser.
image-collage.faq.q5: What if I choose fewer images than there are cells?
image-collage.faq.a5: Images are repeated to fill every cell. If no image is chosen, the cells show their numbers.

exif-remove.pick: Choose one or more images (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC…)
exif-remove.how: Hidden data is stripped from JPG and PNG images without recompressing, so quality stays the same. Other formats are redrawn as high-quality JPG.
exif-remove.hasGps: This photo has GPS coordinates: whoever receives it can tell where it was taken!
exif-remove.fail: Could not process "{n}". Your browser may not be able to read this format.
exif-remove.seo.how1: Photos taken with a phone usually contain EXIF data: camera make and model, date and time, settings and even the GPS coordinates of where it was taken. Anyone who receives the original file could find out where you live.
exif-remove.seo.how2: Choose one or more images and the tool shows everything it finds, raises a red warning if there is GPS data and lets you see the location on a map.
exif-remove.seo.how3: Click Remove data to download a clean copy. For JPG and PNG the data is stripped separately so the image keeps its quality; other formats are saved again as high-quality JPG.
exif-remove.faq.q1: Do Facebook and WhatsApp remove GPS automatically?
exif-remove.faq.a1: Most social networks strip EXIF when you post, but sending a photo as a file by email, WhatsApp (as a document) or Telegram keeps it intact.
exif-remove.faq.q2: Does removing EXIF make the photo rotate wrongly?
exif-remove.faq.a2: JPG photos use orientation data to rotate. If the photo ends up sideways after cleaning, rotate it again with the Crop Image tool.
exif-remove.faq.q3: Does it work on an iPhone?
exif-remove.faq.a3: Yes. Open the page in Safari and pick photos from your library. HEIC photos are saved as JPG.
exif-remove.faq.a4: No. Images are read and processed on your device.
exif-remove.faq.q5: How do I turn off GPS when taking photos?
exif-remove.faq.a5: In the Camera app's location permission settings, choose Never.

voice-recorder.note: Recordings stay only in your browser until you download them, and closing the page loses them. Download WAV to open in any software, or the original format (WebM/MP4) for a smaller file.
voice-recorder.micErr: Could not open the microphone. Allow the browser to use your microphone (lock icon next to the address bar) and check that it is plugged in.
voice-recorder.wavErr: Your browser couldn't convert to WAV. Download the original instead.
voice-recorder.seo.howTitle: How to record audio in your browser
voice-recorder.seo.how1: Click Start recording and allow your browser to use the microphone. A waveform appears so you know the mic is picking up sound; you can pause and then continue in the same recording.
voice-recorder.seo.how2: Turn on Noise reduction and Echo cancellation for a clearer voice in a noisy room, and turn them off when recording instruments to keep the sound natural.
voice-recorder.seo.how3: Each recording can be played back and downloaded as WAV (opens in any software, larger size) or in the original WebM/MP4 format (compact).
voice-recorder.faq.a1: There is no hard limit. One hour of WebM audio is about 30 MB, and WAV is much larger.
voice-recorder.faq.a2: No. The audio stays in your browser until you download it.
voice-recorder.faq.q3: Do I lose recordings if I close the page?
voice-recorder.faq.a3: Yes. Download them before closing or reloading the page.
voice-recorder.faq.q4: How do I get an MP3 file?
voice-recorder.faq.a4: Download the WAV, then use the audio and video trim and convert tool to convert it to MP3.
voice-recorder.faq.q5: Why isn't any sound being recorded?
voice-recorder.faq.a5: Check the microphone permission at the lock icon next to the address bar, and choose the right microphone in your system settings.

speed-test.how: The test downloads sample data through the nearest server of the Cloudflare network (speed.cloudflare.com, free). Each test uses about 50-150 MB of data, so if you are on 4G watch your data plan. Results are for reference and may differ from your carrier's app.
speed-test.p.done: Done. The big number is your download speed.
speed-test.v.great: Very fast: 4K video, online gaming and group video calls are all comfortable.
speed-test.v.good: Good: Full HD/4K video and video calls run smoothly.
speed-test.v.ok: Average: HD video and video calls work, but large downloads are a little slow.
speed-test.v.slow: Slow: video and online meetings may stutter. Try moving closer to your Wi-Fi router or restarting your modem.
speed-test.fail: Could not run the test: the connection dropped, or an ad blocker / firewall is blocking speed.cloudflare.com. Turn off the blocker and try again.
speed-test.seo.howTitle: How to read your speed test results
speed-test.seo.how1: Download speed determines how fast video streams and files download. Upload matters for video calls, livestreams and sending files. Mbps means millions of bits per second.
speed-test.seo.how2: Latency (ping) is the time a data packet takes to travel there and back. The lower the better for gaming and video calls. Jitter is how much ping fluctuates; when it is high, calls tend to stutter.
speed-test.seo.how3: The tool measures through a Cloudflare server near you. For accurate results, close apps that are downloading and stay close to your Wi-Fi router.
speed-test.faq.a1: About 25 Mbps is enough for 4K video on one device. A busy household should have 100 Mbps or more.
speed-test.faq.q2: Why is my result lower than my plan?
speed-test.faq.a2: It can be due to weak Wi-Fi, many devices sharing the connection, peak hours or international routes. Try plugging in an Ethernet cable to compare.
speed-test.faq.q3: Does testing on 4G use up data?
speed-test.faq.a3: Yes, about 50 to 150 MB each time depending on your connection speed.
speed-test.faq.a4: Under 30 ms is excellent, 30 to 80 ms is fine, and over 150 ms is likely to cause lag in games.
speed-test.faq.q5: Why does it differ from Speedtest or Fast?
speed-test.faq.a5: Each service tests against different servers, so some difference in results is normal.

calendar-print.title: Title (optional)
calendar-print.printNote: Click Print, then choose a printer or "Save as PDF". Choose Letter or A4 paper in landscape orientation for the monthly calendar.
calendar-print.seo.how1: Choose a one-month calendar (large, with note lines, great for the fridge or a desk) or a full-year calendar with 12 months on one page. Set a title such as Family Calendar or Class Schedule.
calendar-print.seo.how2: Turn on lunar dates to see the full moon and new moon days highlighted, calculated for the Vietnam time zone, including leap months. Turn on ISO week numbers when you need them for work planning.
calendar-print.seo.how3: Click Print to print on paper, or choose Save as PDF in the print dialog. Only the calendar is printed, and buttons and menus are hidden automatically.
calendar-print.faq.a1: They are computed with an astronomical algorithm for the UTC+7 time zone, matching the Vietnamese lunar calendar, including leap months.
calendar-print.faq.a2: Holidays are not marked yet. You can write them by hand in the notes area after printing.
calendar-print.faq.q3: Will the yearly calendar fit on one page?
calendar-print.faq.a3: Yes. The yearly calendar arranges 12 months in a grid that fits one portrait page, on Letter or A4.
calendar-print.faq.q4: Should the week start on Monday or Sunday?
calendar-print.faq.a4: The US, Canada and Japan usually start on Sunday, while Europe and most of the world start on Monday. You can choose.
calendar-print.faq.q5: Can I make a calendar for next year?
calendar-print.faq.a5: Yes, enter any year from 1900 to 2199.

John

team-split.hint: Click "Split teams" to shuffle randomly. Click again to split a different way.
team-split.seo.how1: Paste a list of names, one per line. Choose to split by number of teams (for example 3 teams) or by players per team (for example teams of 5), and the tool shuffles randomly and divides evenly.
team-split.seo.how2: The shuffle uses your browser's secure random number generator, so nobody can predict the result. Click Split teams again to shuffle a different way.
team-split.seo.how3: Turn on Pick random captains to mark the first person on each team. Copy the result to send to your class or company group chat.
team-split.faq.q1: How are odd numbers of people handled?
team-split.faq.a1: Teams differ in size by at most one person.
team-split.faq.q2: Can it split by skill level?
team-split.faq.a2: Not yet. Tip: split the strong group and the beginner group separately into the same number of teams, then combine them.
team-split.faq.a3: When Remove duplicate names is on, each name is counted only once.
team-split.faq.q4: Is there a limit on the number of people?
team-split.faq.a4: No meaningful limit. Lists of several thousand names still run fine.
team-split.faq.q5: What if I want to pick just one random person?
team-split.faq.a5: Use the Spin the Wheel or Random Number Picker tool.

electricity-bill.vnNote: Calculated with EVN's tiered retail household electricity tariff, in Vietnamese dong (đ).
electricity-bill.oldIdx: Or enter the old meter reading
electricity-bill.note: Prices exclude VAT; actual bills may differ by a few dong because of rounding. If the meter reading period is not a full month, each tier's allowance is prorated by the number of days.
electricity-bill.src: Tariff per Decision 2892/QĐ-BCT (effective 01/11/2026): tier 1 (0–100 kWh) 1.901 đ, tier 2 (101–200) 2.289 đ, tier 3 (201–400) 2.894 đ, tier 4 (401–700) 3.456 đ, tier 5 (701 and up) 3.844 đ/kWh.
electricity-bill.seo.howTitle: How tiered electricity bills are calculated
electricity-bill.seo.how1: From 01/11/2026, household electricity has 5 tiers: 0–100 kWh at 1.901 đ, 101–200 kWh at 2.289 đ, 201–400 kWh at 2.894 đ, 401–700 kWh at 3.456 đ, and 701 kWh and up at 3.844 đ/kWh (before VAT).
electricity-bill.seo.how2: The kWh used are allocated tier by tier, each tier is multiplied by its unit price and the results are added up, then value-added tax is added (currently 8% or 10% depending on the period).
electricity-bill.seo.how3: The Convert money to kWh tab shows how many kWh a bill amount corresponds to; the Estimate by appliance tab adds up the power rating and hours of use of an air conditioner, refrigerator, water heater and more.
electricity-bill.faq.a1: The standard rate is 10%. During periods of tax reduction under National Assembly resolutions, household electricity is taxed at 8%. Choose the rate shown on your bill.
electricity-bill.faq.q2: How do several households sharing one meter calculate?
electricity-bill.faq.a2: Each tier's allowance is multiplied by the number of households. Enter the number of households sharing the meter to calculate correctly.
electricity-bill.faq.q3: How should a landlord charge tenants for electricity?
electricity-bill.faq.a3: If each room has no separate meter, the landlord may charge at most the tier 3 price per kWh.
electricity-bill.faq.q4: Why does the actual bill differ by a few dong?
electricity-bill.faq.a4: Because of rounding, and because when the reading period is not a full month the allowances are prorated by days.
electricity-bill.faq.q5: Is the old 6-tier tariff still used?
electricity-bill.faq.a5: The 6-tier tariff applies until 31/10/2026. The tool keeps it so you can compare.

sudoku-9x9.seo.how1: Fill the 9x9 grid with digits 1 to 9 so that every row, every column and every 3x3 box contains all 9 digits with no repeats. Every puzzle has exactly one solution.
sudoku-9x9.seo.how2: Start with rows, columns and boxes that already have many digits; use notes mode to pencil in candidates and eliminate them. Hints and error checking help when you are stuck.
sudoku-9x9.seo.how3: The game has 10 levels from easy to hard; winning a level unlocks the next one, and your progress is saved in the browser. Play free on computer and phone, with nothing to install and no account needed.
sudoku-9x9.faq.q1: Does every Sudoku have one solution?
sudoku-9x9.faq.a1: Yes, puzzles are generated to have a single unique solution.
sudoku-9x9.faq.a2: Writing small candidate digits in a cell so you can eliminate them step by step.
sudoku-9x9.faq.q3: How do hard levels differ from easy ones?
sudoku-9x9.faq.a3: Fewer given digits and more advanced solving techniques.
sudoku-9x9.faq.a4: Yes. The game is free and runs right in your browser, with no app to download and no sign-up.
sudoku-9x9.faq.a5: Yes, unlocked levels are saved in your browser; the Unlock all levels button lets you jump straight to the hard levels.

sudoku-16x16.seo.how1: The 16x16 grid is divided into 16 boxes of 4x4; every row, column and box must contain the 16 symbols 1–9 and A–G with no repeats.
sudoku-16x16.seo.how2: Large puzzles need patience: use notes, find cells with only one candidate and symbols that fit in only one place in a row or box.
sudoku-16x16.seo.how3: The game has 10 levels from easy to hard; winning a level unlocks the next one, and your progress is saved in the browser. Play free on computer and phone, with nothing to install and no account needed.
sudoku-16x16.faq.a1: 16 different symbols are needed, so letters follow the digit 9.
sudoku-16x16.faq.q2: How long does a game take?
